title: Requesting an Account Statement of Personal Sender Account Transfer History
content:
A Personal Sender Account holder may request an account statement of their personal transfer history for a period they choose. When the customer requests a statement, it is requested with a statement delivery window — a whole number of Paloma business days — that fixes the delivery due date by which the statement is emailed to the address on the customer profile.

## Fixing the delivery window

The delivery window of a statement is fixed only after the account holds a level whose statement history reaches back to the first day of the period requested.

In other words, the delivery window is not fixed for a period whose first day lies further back than the statement history of the level the account holds; it is fixed once the level held has a statement history reaching back to that first day.

## What a statement request is

One call records one statement request on the account history, dated today, covering the period from the opening day to the closing day given, with the delivery due date by which the statement is emailed to the address on the customer profile. The request is recorded as made through the app. Statements are free of charge, and nothing else on the account changes. The customer sees the request, its reference number and its delivery due date in the app.

## How it is invoked

The statement request is the customer's own act. The agent unlocks the tool `request_account_statement_ee1d8031` (with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool`) and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it in their own app session.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `sender_account_id` | the Personal Sender Account reference number of the account whose history the statement covers, as returned by the Personal Sender Account lookup for this customer | an account reference number |
| `statement_period_start` | the opening day of the period the statement covers, the date the customer chooses | a calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, no time part |
| `statement_period_end` | the closing day of the period the statement covers, the date the customer chooses | a calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, no time part |
| `delivery_window_business_days` | the delivery window, as a whole number of Paloma business days | an integer of 1 or more, no fractional part; the tool applies no rounding |

The delivery due date recorded is the date, in YYYY-MM-DD form on Paloma's operations calendar (US Central Time), reached by counting `delivery_window_business_days` Paloma business days (Monday to Friday, excluding US Federal Reserve holidays) forward from today's date, today not counted.

## Return

A successful call returns a text rendering of a dictionary with these fields: `account_event_id` (the reference number of the statement request), `statement_period_start` and `statement_period_end` (YYYY-MM-DD), `request_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD), `delivery_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the business day by which the statement is emailed) and `status` ("requested" when the request was recorded). A receipt with status "requested" and an `account_event_id` means the statement request now stands on the account history.
